about.title: Oxnard Car Accident Claims
about.longDescription: Oxnard sits where farm roads meet freeway traffic, and that mix shows up in the numbers. In 2025, the city recorded 857 injury collisions, with 1,289 people hurt and 8 lives lost. Public records show the heaviest collision volumes along Saviers Road, Oxnard Boulevard, Rose Avenue, and Ventura Road, and reported crashes cluster on Friday evenings between 5 and 7 p.m., when commuters and weekend traffic overlap. If you were hurt in one of these crashes, the days that follow matter. Photograph the scene, keep every medical record, and hold onto repair estimates. Politely decline when the other driver's insurer asks for a recorded statement; you are not required to give one. California allows two years to file a claim, but the window can shrink to six months when a Ventura County agency or the city itself is involved. LawProactive is a free connection service, not a law firm. We match Oxnard residents with an independent attorney who reviews the facts and works on contingency, meaning no fee unless there is a recovery.

whyChoose.title: Why Oxnard Drivers Turn to LawProactive

items.title: Deadlines Are Tracked From Day One
items.desc: California gives most car accident victims two years to file, yet claims involving a public entity can require notice within six months. The attorney you are matched with will identify which clock applies to your Oxnard crash.

items.title: Partial Fault Does Not End Your Claim
items.desc: Under California's pure comparative fault rule, you can still recover even if you share some blame, with your award reduced by your percentage of responsibility. That matters in disputed intersection and lane-change collisions.

items.title: No Fee Unless You Recover
items.desc: Every attorney in the LawProactive network works on contingency, and there is no cap on non-economic damages like pain and suffering in a standard California car accident case. Our connection service costs you nothing.

items.question: I was hit near Oxnard Boulevard and the other driver's insurer keeps calling. What should I say?
items.answer: You can share your name and basic contact details, but you are not obligated to give a recorded statement, and it is generally wise to decline until you have spoken with an attorney. Adjusters may use casual remarks to reduce or deny your claim. Keep your own notes about the crash and let counsel handle the insurer's questions.

items.question: The crash involved a City of Oxnard or Ventura County vehicle. Does that change anything?
items.answer: Yes. Claims against a government entity in California follow a separate process, and the deadline to file an administrative claim can be as short as six months from the date of the crash. Missing that step can bar the lawsuit entirely, so acting quickly is important. An attorney can confirm which agency is involved and what notice is required.

items.question: What evidence should I gather after a car accident in Oxnard?
items.answer: Take photos of vehicle damage, skid marks, traffic signals, and your injuries before anything is cleaned up or repaired. Collect the other driver's insurance information, witness names, and the police report number. Save every medical bill, prescription receipt, and record of missed work. The sooner these details are preserved, the stronger your claim tends to be.
